title: Register to vote or update a registration
question: How do I register to vote or update my registration in Staunton, and what is the deadline?
office: Voter Registration Office (Director of Elections and General Registrar), appointed by the Staunton Electoral Board
summary: Staunton's Voter Registration Office (the General Registrar, appointed by the Staunton Electoral Board) registers city residents under state law. With a Virginia driver's license or DMV ID you can register, or change your address or name, online on the Department of Elections Citizen Portal. Otherwise mail the state VA-NVRA-1 form, postmarked by the deadline, or hand it in at City Hall, 116 W. Beverley Street. For the November 3, 2026 election the last day to register or update is Friday, October 23, 2026; the registration records are then closed for the 10 days before the election. After that, register in person at the registrar's office during early voting or at your ward's polling place on Election Day, and vote a provisional ballot. A denial can be appealed to the Staunton Circuit Court within 10 days of being notified of it ($10 filing fee).

steps.step: Check that you are eligible to register in Staunton
steps.how: You must be a U.S. citizen and a resident of Virginia and of the City of Staunton. Residence means both a place where you actually live and the intention to remain there (domicile and place of abode, Va. Code § 24.2-101). You must be 18, or 18 by the next general election; at 17 you can register now if you will be 18 by then, and also vote in any primary or special election before it. The city's page says you must not be registered to vote in another state (the Department of Elections words it as not 'registered and plan to vote' in another state). You must not currently be found by a court to lack the capacity to understand the act of voting. The Department of Elections says no one may register or vote while physically incarcerated for a felony; such an application is held until release. Otherwise, the Department says that under a 2026 federal court order only a felony recognized at common law in 1870 takes away the right to vote, and it lists three statutes the Commonwealth treats as matching (Va. Code §§ 18.2-32, 18.2-35 and 18.2-36); for those, the Governor must restore your rights first. The city's page and § 24.2-101 as indexed still say any felony needs restoration (see caveats). The Department of Elections says a college student may choose to register at a campus address; give the dorm or residence hall name with its street address.
steps.quote: Be 18 years of age, or 18 years of age by the next general election;

steps.step: If you are 16 or 17, you can preregister
steps.how: Use the regular registration application, online or on paper (steps s4 to s6). Preregistration does not let you vote until you are 18, except that once you will be 18 by the next general election you may vote in any primary or special election before it.
steps.quote: You may pre-register to vote at age 16 or 17.

steps.step: Confirm that you live inside the City of Staunton, find your ward, and check whether you are already registered
steps.who: Applicant; Voter Registration Office; Virginia Department of Elections
steps.how: Staunton is an independent city with its own General Registrar. If your home is outside the city limits, register with the registrar of the county or city where you live (find it with the Department of Elections local registrar lookup). Inside the city, your home address puts you in one of five voting wards: Ward 1 votes at Third Presbyterian Church, 1313 Barterbrook Road; Ward 2 at Christ United Methodist Church, 1500 Churchville Avenue; Ward 3 at Gypsy Hill Park Gym, 229 116th Regimental Road; Ward 4 at Seventh Day Adventist Church, 1000 North Coalter Street; Ward 5 at Memorial Baptist Church, 224 Taylor Street. Look up your ward through the Department of Elections or the city's GIS map. A home split by a boundary line counts where your bedroom is. Check whether you are already registered on the Citizen Portal, or call the office (540.332.3840).
steps.quote: The City has five voting wards.

steps.step: Register or update online through the Citizen Portal
steps.who: Applicant with a Virginia driver's license or DMV-issued ID card; Virginia Department of Elections; General Registrar
steps.how: Staunton's Voter Registration page sends you to the Department of Elections Citizen Portal to register or update your registration. Complete the electronic application there. You need a Virginia driver's license or other DMV-issued ID, and your Social Security number and DMV customer number must match DMV records; DMV's copy of your signature is used. The Department of Elections sends the completed application to Staunton's registrar within five business days. Without a DMV credential, use the paper form (step s5).
steps.deadline: By the registration deadline: Friday, October 23, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 general and special elections (the records are closed during the 10 days before a primary or general election). The Department of Elections says online applications can be submitted through 11:59 p.m. on the final day of registration.
steps.quote: Applications can also be submitted online directly to the Department of Elections through 11:59 p.m. on the final day of registration for each election.

steps.step: Or mail a paper Virginia Voter Registration Application
steps.how: Download the state form VA-NVRA-1 (Spanish, Vietnamese and Korean versions are linked from the How to Register page), or pick one up at the Voter Registration Office, a public library or a DMV office. Complete every starred item and sign it (an applicant with a physical disability can tick the box on the form instead of signing). Give your full Social Security number if you have one: an application without it is denied. Your residence address cannot be a P.O. box; the form allows a separate mailing address only if your residence cannot receive mail, you are homeless, or you are an overseas citizen or an active-duty member, spouse or dependent, and a qualified protected voter (for example a law-enforcement officer or a person with a protective order) gives a Virginia P.O. box there. Phone and email are optional but help the office reach you. The form says first-time voters who registered by mail must show an acceptable ID in federal elections. Mail it to the Voter Registration Office, P.O. Box 1092, Staunton, VA 24402 (the office's mailing address), or to the Virginia Department of Elections, 1100 Bank Street, Richmond, VA 23219 (the address printed on the form). The federal National Mail Voter Registration Form is also accepted.
steps.deadline: Postmarked no later than the registration deadline (October 23, 2026 for November 3, 2026); the form says at least 11 days before the election. An application with no postmark, or an illegible one, counts if it arrives within five days after the books close (Va. Code § 24.2-416.4(A)). The Department of Elections says one postmarked after the deadline is held and processed after the election.
steps.quote: If mailed, the application must be postmarked no later than the registration deadline.

steps.step: Or hand in your application in person
steps.who: Applicant (or a person delivering it for the applicant); Voter Registration Office; any Virginia general registrar; state-designated voter registration agencies
steps.how: Bring the completed form to the Voter Registration Office in Staunton City Hall, 116 W. Beverley Street, first floor: from the front doors, go down the hall to the counter before Council Chambers on the left. Regular hours are 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. You may also hand it to any general registrar in Virginia, who forwards it to Staunton, or apply at a DMV office, a state-designated agency such as social services or the health department, or an armed forces recruitment office. If a registration drive or another person takes your application, they must give you the receipt from the form and deliver the application within 10 days, or by the deadline if that comes first.
steps.deadline: Received by the deadline. On the final day of registration (Friday, October 23, 2026) the Department of Elections says all registrar offices close at 5:00 p.m.; by law the office must be open at least eight hours that day, and people in line at closing may still apply (Va. Code § 24.2-414).
steps.quote: If delivered in person, either by the applicant or a third party, the application must be received by the deadline.

steps.step: Or register, or change your address, through DMV
steps.who: Applicant; Department of Motor Vehicles; Virginia Department of Elections; General Registrar
steps.how: When you get, renew or replace a Virginia driver's license or ID card (not a driver privilege card), or change the address on it, at a DMV office or on its website, DMV asks whether you are a U.S. citizen and lets you decline to have your information sent for voter registration. If you say you are a citizen, are 17 or older and do not decline, DMV sends your information to the Department of Elections. A new applicant's information goes to the registrar to accept or reject. For a voter who moved within Virginia, it goes to the new locality's registrar as a transfer request.
steps.deadline: The registration deadline (October 23, 2026 for November 3, 2026). No separate DMV cut-off was found.
steps.quote: if the information indicates that the voter has moved within the Commonwealth, the Department of Elections shall transmit the information and the registration record to the appropriate general registrar, who shall treat such transmittal as a request for transfer and process it in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.

steps.step: Military and overseas voters: register with the Federal Post Card Application
steps.who: Active-duty uniformed-service members, their spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living outside the United States, whose Virginia residence is in Staunton
steps.how: The FPCA registers you and requests absentee ballots in one form, for all elections that calendar year and the next. Sign it and mail, email or fax it to the Staunton Voter Registration Office. With a Virginia DMV credential you can instead use the Citizen Portal.
steps.deadline: An application from an active-duty member, or a spouse or dependent living with one, may be accepted after the books close if, because of active duty, they are normally absent from Staunton (Va. Code § 24.2-419); that exception does not reach other overseas citizens. The Department of Elections says their FPCA must still be received by 5:00 p.m. eleven days before the election to get a ballot, except in a qualifying emergency. Overseas citizens who are not military and not yet registered must have the FPCA received by close of business on the final day of registration. Those groups may also register in person through Election Day (Department of Elections).
steps.quote: Active-duty uniformed-service voters, their spouses, and their dependents may register to vote or update their voter registration by mail after the final day of registration using the FPCA, an FWAB, or the Voter Registration and Absentee Ballot applications approved by the State Board of Elections.

steps.step: Update your address or name after a move or a name change
steps.how: Tell the registrar promptly. You can use the Citizen Portal, a DMV address change, the VA-NVRA-1 form, or a letter to the Staunton Voter Registration Office giving your name, enough information to identify you (such as your Social Security number), your current address, your previous address and your signature. State law allows a signed written notice by mail or fax. If you move within Staunton, the registrar enters the new address, moves you to your new ward and sends you confirmation. If you move to Staunton from elsewhere in Virginia, apply here or with any registrar, who forwards it. If you leave Staunton, register in your new locality. If you moved within Virginia and missed the deadline, you may still be able to vote in your old precinct in the next November general election and any election before it, unless your registration has already been transferred or cancelled (Va. Code § 24.2-401, in force until July 1, 2027), or use same-day registration (step s10).
steps.deadline: The same as for registering: October 23, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 election. By law a transfer may be entered at any time the registration records are not closed (Va. Code § 24.2-424(B)); after the deadline, see step s10.
steps.quote: Please note: The deadline to register to vote also applies to updating your voter registration address.

steps.step: Missed the deadline: register in person the same day and vote a provisional ballot
steps.who: Applicant; Voter Registration Office (General Registrar); officers of election; Staunton Electoral Board
steps.how: After the books close you can still register in person (apart from the active-duty mail exception in step s8). During early voting, go to the General Registrar's office in City Hall; the city's How to Vote page gives early voting hours in the City Hall lobby of 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., closed on holidays and in inclement weather. The Department of Elections says registration offices are also open for early voting on Sunday October 18, Saturday October 24, Sunday October 25 and Saturday October 31, 2026, and early voting ends at 5:00 p.m. on October 31. On Election Day (November 3, 2026, polls open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.) go to the polling place for your ward; there is no voting at City Hall that day. You complete a registration form and vote a provisional ballot. The Department of Elections says you are given a notice of the date, time and place where the Electoral Board will decide on it; you may attend but do not have to, and you get written notice if the ballot is not counted. A voter already registered elsewhere in Virginia who is updating may be able to vote a regular ballot instead.
steps.deadline: After October 23, 2026 through Election Day, November 3, 2026 (Department of Elections); by law, up to and including the day of the election (Va. Code § 24.2-420.1(A)).
steps.quote: After the standard registration deadline, eligible individuals may register and vote in person via same day registration.

steps.step: The registrar decides, then confirms or denies the application
steps.how: The registrar must register every qualified Staunton resident who applies on time and in the required way. You should then receive a voter card or other confirmation (it is not photo ID). If nothing arrives within 30 days, contact the office or the Department of Elections, or check the Citizen Portal. A denial notice must be sent in writing, and by email or phone if you gave them, with the reason, a new application and the appeal form.
steps.deadline: A denial notice is due within five days after the denial (Va. Code § 24.2-422(A)). An online application reaches the registrar within five business days (Va. Code § 24.2-416.7(F)). No deadline was found for the registrar to decide an application.
steps.quote: If you do not receive this acknowledgement within 30 days after mailing this form, please contact your city or county voter registration office or the Department of Elections.

steps.step: If denied: correct and resubmit, or appeal to the Staunton Circuit Court
steps.who: Applicant; Voter Registration Office; Clerk of the Staunton Circuit Court; Commonwealth's Attorney for the City of Staunton (defends the petition)
steps.how: If the only problem was a missing signature or a missing item, complete and return the new application sent with the denial, or correct it by phone if the office reaches you. For that or any other denial you may appeal to the court: complete and sign the state Petition for Appeal of Denial of Virginia Voter Registration (the denial notice must include it) and file it with the Clerk of the Staunton Circuit Court, George M. Cochran Judicial Center, 113 E. Beverley Street, Clerk's Office on the third floor. The form says to mail it with the $10 filing fee by check payable to the Clerk of Circuit Court; if you pay at the counter, the Clerk's page says transactions needing payment must be done before 4:30 p.m. The court hears the petition ahead of its other business, and the Commonwealth's Attorney defends. A judgment in your favor entitles you to be registered; a judgment against you can be appealed to the Court of Appeals. The close-of-books rule still applies to a resubmitted application or a petition.
steps.deadline: Within 10 days of being notified of the denial (Va. Code § 24.2-422(B))
steps.fee: $10 filing fee for the court petition; no writ tax or security for costs
steps.quote: A person denied registration shall have the right to appeal, without payment of writ tax or giving security for costs, to the circuit court of the county or city in which he offers to register by filing with the clerk of the court, within 10 days of being notified of the denial, a petition in writing to have his right to register determined.

escalation.trigger: Application denied only for a missing signature or a missing required item
escalation.next: Staunton Voter Registration Office: return the new application sent with the denial notice, or correct it by phone if the office reaches you
escalation.deadline: Before the registration records close; the close-of-books rule applies to a resubmitted application (Va. Code § 24.2-422(C))
escalation.quote: The general registrar shall advise the applicant that he may complete and submit the new application, in lieu of filing an appeal, if the reason stated for denial is that the applicant has failed to sign the application or failed to provide a required item of information on the application.

escalation.trigger: Registration denied (or a second application denied)
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court, by petition filed with the Clerk; the Commonwealth's Attorney defends and the hearing takes precedence over other business
escalation.deadline: Within 10 days of being notified of the denial
escalation.quote: A person denied registration shall have the right to appeal, without payment of writ tax or giving security for costs, to the circuit court of the county or city in which he offers to register by filing with the clerk of the court, within 10 days of being notified of the denial, a petition in writing to have his right to register determined.

escalation.trigger: The Circuit Court rules against the petitioner
escalation.deadline: Notice of appeal within 30 days from the date of the final judgment order (Va. Code § 8.01-675.3)
escalation.quote: From a judgment rendered against the petitioner, an appeal shall lie to the Court of Appeals.

escalation.trigger: No confirmation and no denial notice received (application apparently not acted on)
escalation.next: Staunton Voter Registration Office (540.332.3840, vote@ci.staunton.va.us), then the Virginia Department of Elections
escalation.deadline: A denial notice is due within five days of a denial (Va. Code § 24.2-422(A)); the Department of Elections suggests following up if no acknowledgement arrives within 30 days
escalation.quote: If you believe you have been wrongfully denied registration and have not received any communication, please contact the general registrar for the city or county where you live or the Department of Elections for immediate assistance.

escalation.trigger: Unhappy with how the office handled a registration (delay, lost application, service)
escalation.next: Staunton Voter Registration Office first; then the Staunton Electoral Board, which appoints the General Registrar (StauntonElectoralBoard@ci.staunton.va.us)
escalation.quote: Localities are primarily responsible for responding to all voter complaints they receive and may request board staff for assistance as needed.

escalation.trigger: Problem not resolved locally, or a time-critical registration problem
escalation.next: Virginia Department of Elections: informal complaint on the online form or by phone ((800) 552-9745); the online form also notifies the Staunton registrar
escalation.quote: The online complaint form will notify the Department of Elections and the General Registrar of the locality where the incident occurred of what has happened.

escalation.trigger: A violation of Title III of the Help America Vote Act (which covers the statewide voter registration list and the contents of registration forms)
escalation.next: Virginia Department of Elections: formal complaint on the notarized ELECT-15512 form mailed to the Deputy Commissioner; hearing on request; alternative dispute resolution if not resolved within 90 days
escalation.deadline: Within 10 days of the incident; final determination within 90 days of receipt of the complaint (Department of Elections)
escalation.quote: You have 10 days from the date of the incident to file a complaint.

escalation.trigger: Disagree with the Commissioner's final determination on a formal complaint
escalation.next: State Board of Elections (it may hold a hearing or rely on the record, and decides within 45 days)
escalation.quote: The Commissioner’s final determination may be appealed to the full State Board of Elections within 15 days.

escalation.trigger: Repeated neglect of a clear ministerial duty by the registrar (for example, applications persistently not processed)
escalation.next: Staunton Electoral Board or State Board of Elections. After a public hearing, either may vote by recorded majority to institute removal proceedings in the Staunton Circuit Court, or remove the registrar itself (the Electoral Board by unanimous vote, with appeal to the State Board; the State Board by a two-thirds vote). The statutes read give these steps to the boards, not to individual voters, who can only raise the matter with them.
escalation.quote: A general registrar may be removed or have removal proceedings instituted against him pursuant to this subsection for (i) neglect of a clear, ministerial duty of the office, misuse of the office, or incompetence in the performance of the duties of the office where such neglect, misuse, or incompetence has a material adverse effect upon the conduct of the office

escalation.trigger: Suspected unlawful conduct under the election laws, such as a false statement on a registration application or an application a drive failed to deliver
escalation.next: Commonwealth's Attorney for the City of Staunton
escalation.quote: Any complaint or allegation concerning unlawful conduct under this title shall be filed with the attorney for the Commonwealth of the county or city in which the alleged violation occurred.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. Later copies of the Voter Registration page replay its 2026-05-07 copy, and the Electoral Board page's 2026-05-13 copy redirects to that of 2025-01-30. The old addresses /i-want-to/register-to-vote and /residents/voting-information only redirect to the Voter Registration page. The city's Web Disclaimer & Privacy Policy sets no limit on reusing page content. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

Deadline for November 3, 2026. The newest captured Voter Registration page (2026-05-07) gives only the August 4, 2026 primary deadline (July 24, 2026) and says of the November 3 election 'Stay tuned for deadline information and a sample ballot.' The October 23, 2026 deadline here comes from the Department of Elections Upcoming Elections page, read on 2026-10-11 ('Register to Vote/Update Registration: 10/23/2026'). It matches Va. Code § 24.2-416(A) as amended in 2025: the records are closed during the 10 days before a primary or general election, so the last day is the 11th day before. The live Registrar page's own November deadline is not confirmed.

Special-election deadlines differ between Department of Elections pages. 'How to Register' gives 14 days before a special election and 7 days before one called by the Governor. 'Registration' gives 11 and 7 days. 'View Your Info' still says changes cannot be made 'during the 21 day period before any general or primary election or during the 12 day period before a special election', and the Same Day Voter Registration page still speaks of the old 21-day closure and an 'October 24 deadline' from an earlier year. Under § 24.2-416(A) the records close during the 6 days before a special election called by the Governor, the Speaker, the President pro tempore or a house of the General Assembly, and during the 10 days before any other special election, unless already closed for a primary or general election. This page follows the statute and the Department's current Upcoming Elections page; confirm special-election dates with the office.

Felony convictions. The city's How to Vote page (May 2026 capture) still lists 'Have your voting rights restored if you've been convicted of a felony;' as a requirement, and Va. Code § 24.2-101 as indexed still says no person convicted of a felony is a qualified voter unless civil rights are restored. The Department of Elections says that, under a 2026 federal court order, only felonies recognized at common law in 1870 disqualify (it lists §§ 18.2-32, 18.2-35 and 18.2-36), that other rights return on release, and that an applicant who need not apply for restoration should answer 'yes' to the felony question and 'no' to the restoration question. The order was not read and the legal position may change; applicants should ask the office.

Same-day registration. The provisional ballot comes from the Department of Elections' procedures (§ 24.2-420.1(B)), its Same Day Voter Registration page and the city's How to Vote page; no statute in the index requiring a provisional ballot for same-day registrants was found. The city's pages read do not give Staunton's weekend early-voting hours for November 2026 (the May capture gives weekend hours only for the August primary, and says the office is open on the Saturday before all general elections from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.); the weekend dates in step s10 are the Department of Elections' statewide ones. That same-day registration is offered during every early-voting hour is an inference. Section 24.2-420.1(A) allows in-person registration at the registrar's office up to and including Election Day, but the city and the Department of Elections describe it only during early voting (which ends at 5:00 p.m. on Saturday, October 31) and at the polling place on Election Day; whether the office takes same-day registrations on Monday, November 2, was not found. The How to Vote page places early voting in the 'City Hall Lobby' and same-day registration at 'the General Registrar's office'; both are in City Hall.

Fax and email. The Voter Registration page publishes a phone number and an office mailbox (vote@ci.staunton.va.us) but no fax number. The Department of Elections 'View Your Info' page says the update form 'may be faxed', and Va. Code §§ 24.2-423 and 24.2-424(A) allow a written name or address notice by mail or facsimile; whether the Staunton office accepts registration updates by email was not found. FPCAs may be emailed or faxed (Department of Elections Military & Overseas page).

Mailing address. P.O. Box 1092, Staunton, VA 24402 is the address in the office's contact block, and the How to Vote page gives it for mailed absentee ballot applications. No page read says in so many words to mail registration applications there; the Department of Elections says to mail them to the local registrar (or to the Department in Richmond, the address printed on the form).

Forms. The VA-NVRA-1 file is named rev-6-2025 but its footer reads 'VA-NVRA-1 05/2025'. Its text layer is partial (the postmark-day figure does not extract), so the '11 days' in step 5, the Box 4 mailing-address rule and the first-time mail registrant ID note are transcriptions from the page image, which a text search cannot confirm. The Petition for Appeal (f5) is a scanned image with no text layer; its fee sentence is a transcription from the page image too. That petition has five fillable text fields (court address, city or county, petitioner name, registrar's city or county, facts) and no signature field, but it prints a 'Signed' line for the petitioner and says 'Complete and sign the petition and mail it with your check', so it must be printed and signed; it is marked fillable here (Albemarle's page marks the same form as not fillable). VA-NVRA-1 has no form fields. ELECT-15512 declares an AcroForm but has no fields. The FPCA link the Department publishes (fpca2013.pdf) leads to a PDF whose edition may be dated.

The appeal form says the appeal must be received by the Clerk 'no later than ten days after the date shown on the reverse side of this form'. The PDF has one page and no reverse side; the statute counts 10 days from being notified of the denial.

Fees. No source read (state law, the city's pages or the Department of Elections pages) sets or mentions a fee for registering or updating a registration, so none is recorded; no source saying registration is free was found either. Circuit Court costs beyond the $10 filing fee, and Court of Appeals fees, are not covered here.

Local law. No Staunton ordinance on voter registration was found; registration is governed by Title 24.2 and State Board rules. The City Code is on General Code's eCode360, whose terms forbid reproducing its content for public purposes, so only the tables of contents of the Charter and of Title 2 (Administration) were read. Title 2 has no elections chapter, and the ordinance establishing the wards and polling places that Va. Code § 24.2-307 requires was not located. The Charter section on wards is quoted from the Charter as published by the General Assembly's Legislative Information System (law.lis.virginia.gov), an official source. Charter § 4.1 has council members elected at large; the Where to Vote page treats each ward as a voting precinct ('You must appear at your assigned precinct to vote on Election Day').

Wards and polling places come from the 2026-05-10 capture of the Where to Vote page and may have changed. The city's GIS map, the Department of Elections polling-place lookup and the Citizen Portal and registrar lookup on vote.elections.virginia.gov are not described here (the last refuses automated readers). Their functions are described from www.elections.virginia.gov pages.

Electoral Board. The newest playable capture of its page is from 2025-01-30; it lists one scheduled meeting (February 5, 2025) and says members serve three-year terms. Whether the Board takes public comment from voters was not found. The page lists members by name with personal mailboxes; only the board mailbox is recorded.

Privacy: the Voter Registration page names the Director of Elections and General Registrar, the Electoral Board page names its members with personal city mailboxes, and the Clerk's, court's and Commonwealth's Attorney's pages name officers, judges and staff. None of these is recorded; only office channels are listed (vote@ and StauntonElectoralBoard@ are office mailboxes).

Circuit Court address. The city's Clerk page gives the George M. Cochran Judicial Center, 3rd Floor, 113 E. Beverley Street. The Virginia court system page gives the address '113 East Beverley Street' on one line and '2nd Floor' on the next, then 'Clerk's Office - Third Floor', with the same phone (540) 332-3874 and Clerk's Office hours 8:30AM - 5:00PM.

Versions. In the index, Va. Code §§ 24.2-101, 24.2-404, 24.2-418 and 24.2-427 carry contingent effective or expiration notes (Acts 2026, cc. 992 and 1081); § 24.2-401 (voting in the old precinct after a move) and § 24.2-444 are marked effective until July 1, 2027. The index holds only the contingent-effective version of § 24.2-418 (LIS shows a version in force now and versions taking effect January 1, 2027 or on the contingency); the three sentences quoted from it are word for word the same in the version now in force, checked on LIS on 2026-10-11. Re-check these sections after those dates.

Appeal window wording. The Department of Elections Voter Complaints page says the appeal 'must be filed within 10 days after the denial'; § 24.2-422(B) counts 10 days from being notified of the denial. This page follows the statute; filing within 10 days of the denial itself is the safe course.

Not modelled here: absentee voting by mail and early voting themselves (separate processes), the Officer of Election application, and voter photo ID rules. A voter card or confirmation is not photo identification (Department of Elections).

Not confirmed by lexflow's software: the words once quoted for the fee 'Circuit Court petition appealing a registration denial: how to pay (state appeal form)' (https://www.elections.virginia.gov/media/formswarehouse/veris-voter-registration/applications/AppealOfDenialRequest.pdf) were not found on the cited page as lexflow read it (the cited page could not be read (the PDF has no text layer lexflow can read); the form is a scan with no text layer, so a text search cannot read it). Those claims now rest on the cited page as read, without a matched quote; check them at the link before relying on them.

corrections: Quotes: all 86 structured quotes were re-checked and none was removed. The 63 state-law quotes (54 in legal_basis, steps s7 and s12, fees 1 and 3, escalation rungs 1, 2, 3, 9 and 10) are substrings of I.text_of for their cited sections after whitespace-only normalisation, and each subsection label matches the text. The 22 quotes from official pages (city How to Vote and Where to Vote, read from the cited Internet Archive captures because www.ci.staunton.va.us still returns HTTP 403 to the research client, robots.txt included; Department of Elections State-designated Voter Registration, How to Register, Military & Overseas, View Your Info and Voter Complaints; 1VAC20-40-30 and 1VAC20-20-80 on LIS; Staunton Charter § 12 on LIS) match copies fetched on 2026-10-11. The f5 fee sentence was confirmed word for word from the decoded page image of the scanned PDF. Quoted fragments in caveats and step text were also checked; one ('113 East Beverley Street, 2nd Floor') added a comma that is not on the court page and was rewritten.

Summary: 'the deadline is Friday, October 23, 2026' now says October 23 is the last day to register or update and the records are then closed for the 10 days before the election (Va. Code §§ 24.2-414, 24.2-416(A)). The appeal window now runs from being notified of the denial, as in § 24.2-422(B).

s1: the draft said 'not registered or planning to vote in another state', which widens the rule; the city says 'Not be registered to vote in another state' and the Department of Elections 'Not be registered and plan to vote in another state', and the step now gives both. 'By the next November general election' is now 'by the next general election' (§ 24.2-403, city and Department wording). Residence now gives both domicile and place of abode (§ 24.2-101). The incarceration rule, the 1870 common-law felony test, the three listed statutes and the campus-address option are attributed to the Department of Elections, with its note that an incarcerated applicant's application is held until release and the dorm-name instruction.

s5: added from the state form and § 24.2-418: the physical-disability exception to signing, when a separate mailing address may be given (Box 4) and the protected-voter Virginia P.O. box, and the form's note that first-time voters who registered by mail must show ID in federal elections.
s7: added from § 24.2-411.3(A) and (C) that driver privilege cards are excluded and that DMV sends information only for a person who says he is a citizen, is 17 or older and does not decline.

s8: the deadline said active-duty members and families 'may register after the books close'. § 24.2-419 says such an application 'may be accepted' notwithstanding § 24.2-416, only if by reason of active duty they are normally absent from the locality, and the exception does not reach subdivision 3 (persons temporarily outside the United States). The text now keeps the 'may', the condition and the limit.

s9: the letter now includes a signature (Department of Elections View Your Info; § 24.2-424(A) requires a signed written notice, by mail or fax). The old-precinct rule now keeps the statute's limit 'unless his registration has been transferred or cancelled' (§ 24.2-401). The deadline said a transfer can be entered 'only while' the records are open; § 24.2-424(B) says it 'may be entered in the registration records at any time the registration records are not closed', and same-day registration operates notwithstanding § 24.2-416, so the text now quotes the statute's sense and points to s10.

s10: 'only in person' now notes the active-duty mail exception (§ 24.2-419). 'A written notice' of the Electoral Board meeting was not on any page; the Department of Elections says 'a notice with the date, time, and place', and adds written notice if the ballot is not counted. The text now follows it.

s12: the appeal is available for any denial, not only 'otherwise'. Added from the form that the petition must be completed and signed (it prints a signature line) and mailed with the check, and from § 24.2-422(B) that the denial notice must include the form.

Escalation rung 8: added that either board may, after a public hearing, also remove the registrar itself (the Electoral Board by unanimous vote with appeal to the State Board, § 24.2-109(B); the State Board by a two-thirds vote, § 24.2-103(E)). 'A resident ... cannot start the proceedings' was an inference; it now says the statutes read give these steps to the boards, not to individual voters.

Caveats: added that the index holds only the contingent-effective version of § 24.2-418 and that the three quoted sentences are identical in the version now in force on LIS; that the Department of Elections Voter Complaints page counts the appeal window from the denial while the statute counts from notice; that whether same-day registration is offered on Monday, November 2, was not found; and the f5 signature line. The verifier rendered VA-NVRA-1 page 2 and confirmed the '11 days' figure and the 05/2025 footer. Added the LIS § 24.2-418 page to sources.
1 quote lexflow's software could not find on the cited pages as it read them on 2026-10-20 (listed in 'removed') dropped from the claims and noted in the caveats; every other quote matched.
open_issues: www.ci.staunton.va.us still returns HTTP 403 to the research client (robots.txt included), so every city fact comes from Internet Archive captures (Voter Registration 2026-05-07, How to Vote 2026-05-11, Where to Vote 2026-05-10, Clerk of Circuit Court 2026-07-21, Commonwealth's Attorney 2026-02-15, Electoral Board 2025-01-30). Ward polling places, office hours and the city's November 2026 weekend early-voting hours were not confirmed on the live pages. The October 23, 2026 deadline rests on the Department of Elections Upcoming Elections page and § 24.2-416(A), not on a city page.

City Code not read: eCode360's terms were respected and only tables of contents were read. No Staunton ordinance on registration was found, and the ward and polling-place ordinance required by § 24.2-307 was not located.

The Citizen Portal and the registrar lookup on vote.elections.virginia.gov were not read (its robots.txt disallows all automated access), so the 11:59 p.m. online cut-off on the final registration day rests on the Department of Elections' State-designated Voter Registration page.

Felony eligibility is unsettled in the sources: the Department of Elections cites a 2026 federal court order limiting disqualifying felonies, while § 24.2-101 as indexed and the city's How to Vote page still require restoration of rights for any felony. The order itself was not read; s1 attributes the rule to the Department and points to the caveat.

Same-day registration: whether the office takes same-day registrations on Monday, November 2, after early voting ends, and during every early-voting hour, was not confirmed. No statute in the index requiring a provisional ballot for same-day registrants was found; the rule comes from Department of Elections procedures and pages.
Not confirmed: whether the Staunton office accepts registration updates by fax or email (no fax number is published).

Special-election deadlines differ between Department of Elections pages (14, 11 and 7 days, and 21 and 12 days on older pages); the caveat gives the statutory periods. The steps cover the November 3, 2026 election.

Visual-only PDF readings: the f5 fee sentence, signature instruction and reverse-side wording (scanned image), and the f1 postmark figure and footer (partial text layer, read from a rendered page). The FPCA PDF and the EAC page were not opened.

No deadline was found for the registrar to decide an application. Circuit Court costs beyond the $10 filing fee and Court of Appeals fees were not researched, and whether the Electoral Board takes public comment was not found.
